national.name: StrongHearts Native Helpline
national.description: 24/7 confidential helpline by and for Native Americans and Alaska Natives affected by domestic, dating, and sexual violence.
national.text: Text START to 1-844-762-8483, or chat via strongheartshelpline.org

national.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
national.description: Free, confidential support for anyone in suicidal crisis or emotional distress, and for people worried about a loved one.
national.text: Text 988, or chat at chat.988lifeline.org (Spanish, LGBTQI+, and Deaf/HoH options available)

national.name: Crisis Text Line
national.description: Free 24/7 text-based support with a trained crisis counselor for any kind of crisis.
national.text: Text HOME to 741741 (HOLA for Spanish); WhatsApp 1-443-787-7678; chat at connect.crisistextline.org

national.name: National Domestic Violence Hotline
national.description: 24/7 confidential support, safety planning, and local referrals for anyone experiencing domestic violence or abuse.
national.text: Text START to 88788, or chat at thehotline.org

national.name: RAINN National Sexual Assault Hotline
national.description: Free, confidential 24/7 support for survivors of sexual assault and their loved ones, in English and Spanish.
national.text: Text HOPE to 64673, or chat at rainn.org/hotline (Signal messaging also available)

national.name: National Human Trafficking Hotline
national.description: 24/7 confidential help and tip line for victims and survivors of sex or labor trafficking, and for reporting suspected trafficking.

national.name: NamUs (National Missing & Unidentified Persons System)
national.description: Free national database where families can enter a missing loved one's case once a police report exists; cases are vetted with the investigating agency, and NamUs provides free forensic services including family DNA kits.
national.text: Create a case or send questions via the web form at namus.nij.ojp.gov/contact (choose Case Support)

national.name: National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC)
national.description: 24-hour hotline for reporting and finding missing children and teens under 18 — call right after 911.

national.name: BIA Missing & Murdered Unit (MMU)
national.description: Federal unit that analyzes and helps solve missing and murdered cases involving American Indians and Alaska Natives — families can submit case information or tips by phone, email (OJS_MMU@bia.gov), or online form.
national.text: Submit a tip or case online at bia.gov/service/mmu/submit-tip-or-case-information

national.name: FBI Tips
national.description: Report a federal crime or share information on a missing or murdered loved one's case with the FBI by phone or online.
national.text: Submit a tip online at tips.fbi.gov

california.name: California DOJ Missing Persons Section
california.description: The state's missing persons clearinghouse — searchable database, free DNA program for families, and confirmation that there is NO waiting period to report someone missing in California (missing.persons@doj.ca.gov).

california.name: Feather Alert (California Highway Patrol)
california.description: California's emergency alert for missing Indigenous people in danger — ask the investigating law enforcement agency to request activation from CHP; if police make no determination within 24 hours, the person's tribe may request it from CHP directly.

california.name: CA DOJ Office of Native American Affairs (ONAA)
california.description: The Attorney General's tribal liaison office — leads the state's MMIP outreach, Missing in California Indian Country events, and tribal community response planning (ONAA@doj.ca.gov).

california.name: Yurok Tribal Court MMIP Program (To' Kee Skuy' Soo Ney-Wo-Chek')
california.description: Tribal MMIP program serving Northern California families — case and tip intake, search assistance, advocacy, accompaniment, and support with reunification costs.
california.text: Anonymous case and tip forms at yuroktribalcourt.org
california.address: 230 Klamath Blvd. Ste. A, Klamath, CA

california.name: California Victim Compensation Board (CalVCB)
california.description: State program that reimburses crime-related expenses for victims and families, such as counseling, medical care, and funeral or burial costs.

california.name: 211 California
california.description: Free, confidential referrals to local food, housing, health, mental health, and crisis services anywhere in California.
california.text: Text your ZIP code to 898211 (where available)
california.hours: 24/7 in most counties (13 rural counties lack full 24/7 service)

california.name: California Tribal Families Coalition (CTFC)
california.description: Statewide coalition of California tribes advocating for the health, safety, and welfare of tribal children and families (contact@caltribalfamilies.org).

california.name: California Indian Legal Services (CILS)
california.description: Free or low-cost legal help for Native individuals and tribes in every California county, with offices in Escondido, Sacramento, Bishop, and Eureka.

california.name: California Rural Indian Health Board (CRIHB)
california.description: Statewide network of tribal health programs promoting the health and social conditions of California's Indian people, including domestic violence prevention.

california.name: California Consortium for Urban Indian Health (CCUIH)
california.description: Statewide association of ten urban Indian health programs offering culturally centered care, with violence-prevention work through its Red Women Rising program.
california.address: 1900 Point West Way, Ste. 111, Sacramento, CA 95815
